metaData.title: The Ironies of A^2 I^2
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This talk explores the enduring ironies of automation and AI in incident response, arguing that while these technologies offer autonomy and authority, they lack directed attention, redirectability, and interpredictability, which are crucial for human coordination and can lead to severe failures in high-stakes contexts.
metaData.summary: J. Paul Reed's presentation, based on foundational human factors research from 1983 (Bainbridge) and recent AI-specific work (Endsley, 2024), examines how automation and AI introduce paradoxical challenges during incident response. Key ironies include skill degradation from disuse, the opacity of AI decision-making, and the inability to redirect automated agents. Reed highlights that automation and AI possess autonomy and authority but lack the human cognitive faculties of directed attention, redirectability, and interpredictability, which are the foundations of effective coordination. He shares real-world incident stories where AI agents ignored explicit instructions, generated code that caused new incidents, and provided unhelpful distractions in critical communication channels. The talk introduces the Efficiency-Thoroughness Trade-Off (ETTO) principle, noting that responders in incidents have already lost the efficiency bet. Citing a 2025 study, Reed shows that while AI can improve performance by 53-67% when correct, it can degrade performance by 96-120% when misleading. The conclusion emphasizes the need to cultivate practices that 'buy time' in incidents, such as simulations and chaos engineering, and to maintain broad mental models of systems rather than relying solely on AI's opaque models.

mainPoints.point: Automation and AI lack the human cognitive foundations for coordination: directed attention, redirectability, and interpredictability.
mainPoints.explanation: While automation has autonomy and authority, it cannot be asked what it is focusing on, cannot be redirected to a new priority, and its actions become unpredictable in novel situations, breaking the coordination needed for effective incident response.

mainPoints.point: The ironies of automation from 1983 remain critically relevant to modern AI systems.
mainPoints.explanation: Issues like skill degradation, the need for deep system knowledge to generate new strategies, and the speed-versus-correctness tradeoff are amplified by AI's opacity and non-deterministic nature.

mainPoints.point: AI's performance in high-stakes settings is brittle: it can significantly help when correct but catastrophically hinder when wrong.
mainPoints.explanation: A 2025 study showed nurses performed 53-67% better with accurate AI predictions but 96-120% worse with misleading ones, highlighting the severe downside risk of relying on AI during incidents.

mainPoints.point: Effective incident response requires cultivating the ability to 'buy time' and maintain broad mental models, not outsourcing them to AI.
mainPoints.explanation: Practices like simulations and chaos engineering build maneuverability. Relying on AI's opaque model prevents responders from building the deep system understanding needed to detect and correct AI hallucinations.

keyQuotes: The more advanced control system is, the more crucial may be the contribution of the human operator.
Technologists often mistake connectivity, the capability to connect disparate parties and data sources for coordination.
When AI predictions were most misleading, those nurses performed at 96% to 120% worse than when they worked without AI assistance.
When it's good, it's a little good... When it's bad, it can be really bad.
I think one of the siren songs of AI is, the AI has the model, so I don't have to keep it in my head.

relatedArticles.title: Introducing Claude Opus 4.7
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Anthropic has released Claude Opus 4.7, a significant upgrade over Opus 4.6 with major improvements in advanced software engineering, vision capabilities, instruction following, and autonomous long-horizon reasoning, while implementing new cyber safeguards and maintaining the same pricing.

relatedArticles.title: Introducing GPT-5.5
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI releases GPT-5.5, its most capable model yet, with significant gains in agentic coding, knowledge work, and scientific research, while maintaining GPT-5.4 latency and improving token efficiency.

relatedArticles.title: 4 Patterns of AI Native Development
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Patrick Debois outlines four evolving patterns of AI-native development—shifting from producer to manager, implementation to intent, delivery to discovery, and content to knowledge.

relatedArticles.title: Sam Altman + Greg Brockman - On The Great OpenAI Reset
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Sam Altman and Greg Brockman discuss OpenAI's journey, the shift towards personal AGI and agent infrastructure, the jagged frontier of AI capabilities, and the societal implications of abundant compute and intelligence.

relatedArticles.title: MCP in the Java World: Bringing Architectural Strategy to LLM Integrations
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: MCP Java SDK transforms LLM integration from ad-hoc tool calling into a disciplined architectural pattern, introducing protocol-level contracts, anti-corruption layers, and governance for enterprise Java systems.

relatedArticles.title: What I Learned Building Multi-Agent Systems From Scratch
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A staff engineer at Shopify shares the journey of building multi-agent systems from scratch, revealing that narrow-focused agents outperform generalists, and that empowering domain experts with tools is more effective than creating an AI SWAT team.

relatedArticles.title: Engineering at AI Speed: Lessons from the First Agentically Accelerated Software Project
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article presents a case study of building Claude Code using Claude Code, detailing three stories that illustrate how AI changes bottlenecks in the software development lifecycle, emphasizing experimentation, architectural choices, and the importance of shipping to discover real requirements.

relatedArticles.title: Anthropic Introduces Project Glasswing and Claude Mythos Preview
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Anthropic launches Project Glasswing, a software security initiative powered by their new frontier model, Claude Mythos Preview, designed to identify critical vulnerabilities.

relatedArticles.title: Claude Code auto mode: a safer way to skip permissions
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Claude Code's new Auto mode uses a two-stage model-based classifier and prompt-injection probes to autonomously gate dangerous actions, balancing developer productivity with security.

relatedArticles.title: Using AI as a Thinking Partner for Large-Scale Engineering Systems
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A Google Senior Staff Engineer shares a structured methodology for using AI as a thinking partner to understand, experiment with, and redesign a complex, multi-language, multi-repository engineering system.
